chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of his companions, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about divorce when one does not divorce according to the waiting period ('iddah). So he said: 'He is referred back to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.الطَّلَاق: Talaq — the Islamic institution of divorce, specifically the pronouncement formula. In Shia jurisprudence, divorce must meet strict conditions to be valid.
key_terms.الْعِدَّة: 'Iddah — the mandatory waiting period a woman must observe after divorce before she may remarry. Surat al-Talaq (65:1) stipulates divorce must be pronounced at the beginning of the 'iddah.
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — honorific epithet for God, commonly used after mentioning Allah in hadith texts.
key_terms.يُرَدُّ إِلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: He is referred back to the Book of Allah — the Imam's jurisprudential principle that invalid acts must be measured against Quranic standards.

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about divorce pronounced outside the waiting period ('iddah)?
ai.summary: A narrator asks Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the validity of a divorce pronounced outside the prescribed waiting period ('iddah). The Imam's ruling is direct and authoritative: such a divorce must be referred back to the Book of Allah — meaning it is invalid and must conform to the Quranic regulations in Surat al-Talaq (65:1), which explicitly stipulates that divorce must be pronounced during a period of purity. This response reflects the Imam's method of directing legal questions back to the Quran as the supreme source of jurisprudential rulings.
